tldr: Three reinforcement-learning items landed over two weeks: an InfoQ talk on OpenAI's Agent RFT fine-tuning platform, and two arXiv papers applying RL to fraud detection and federated microgrid coordination. The items share a topic, not a storyline — each is a standalone read, not a developing event.
whats_new: The latest addition is an arXiv paper proposing constraint-aware aggregation for federated RL, replacing standard FedAvg so microgrid energy-coordination agents respect system-level constraints instead of just averaging local updates.
why_it_matters: For platform engineers running RL fine-tuning, the InfoQ talk is the practical read on OpenAI's managed Agent RFT platform; the two arXiv papers are narrower academic results (fraud detection, energy-grid coordination) with no direct deployment path.

beats.headline: InfoQ talk details OpenAI's Agent RFT fine-tuning platform
beats.summary: Conference presentation on fine-tuning reasoning models via real-time tool interactions and custom reward signals.

beats.headline: Semantic Pareto-DQN targets "fraud collapse" in anomaly detection
beats.summary: New multi-objective RL framework aims to fix single-objective algorithms that default to the majority class under extreme class imbalance.

beats.headline: Federated RL paper targets constraint-aware aggregation for microgrids
beats.summary: New arXiv work proposes constraint-aware aggregation to fix standard FedAvg's failure to respect system-level constraints when coordinating distributed energy resources.

open_questions: Does OpenAI's Agent RFT platform get a broader availability announcement beyond this conference talk?
Does the Semantic Pareto-DQN approach get validated outside financial anomaly detection?
Does the constraint-aware federated RL aggregation get tested on a real microgrid deployment, or only in simulation?
take_for_builders: Evaluating OpenAI's managed Agent RFT platform for reasoning-model fine-tuning? Treat the two arXiv papers (fraud-detection Pareto-DQN, federated microgrid RL) as domain-specific research ideas, not production-ready recipes for your own RL training pipeline.
